# CreatorChahiye

> CreatorChahiye (formerly CreatorHive) is a founder-led influencer marketing agency in India for startups and D2C brands. It handles creator discovery, outreach and negotiation, campaign management, UGC, product seeding and reporting, and runs every campaign on a written agreement. It also runs a network of 5,000+ creators (nano to macro) across India.

Key facts:
- Name: CreatorChahiye. Former name: CreatorHive (same company, renamed in 2026). Former domain: creatorhive.in
- Founder: Karan Aryan
- Location served: India
- Contact: karan@creatorchahiye.com, WhatsApp +91 70655 55395
- Clients and work include T-Hub (creator-led startup stories), MI TUBE (creator acquisition and onboarding), Marg (influencer coordination) and Persaura (13-creator jewellery launch)

## Guides
- [Influencer Marketing Cost in India: What to Budget](https://creatorchahiye.com/guides/influencer-marketing-cost-india/): Most Indian brands can run a meaningful micro-influencer campaign from roughly ₹25,000–₹50,000 in creator fees. What you actually pay depends on creator tier, format (Reel, Story, static), usage rights and exclusivity. Agency fees, product seeding and paid boosting come on top.
- [How to Choose Micro-Influencers in India](https://creatorchahiye.com/guides/how-to-choose-micro-influencers/): Choose micro-influencers on audience fit, not follower count. Check who follows them (city, age, interests), whether their engagement looks genuine, whether their content style suits your product, and test with a small paid pilot before scaling.
- [Influencer Marketing for Startups: Where to Start](https://creatorchahiye.com/guides/influencer-marketing-for-startups/): Start with one goal, a small pilot of 5–10 nano and micro creators, a written brief, trackable links or codes, and a two-to-four-week review window. Learn from the pilot, then scale what worked.
- [How Small Creators Get Paid Brand Deals in India](https://creatorchahiye.com/guides/get-paid-brand-collaborations-instagram/): Pick a clear niche, put your audience data in a one-page media kit, set a fair starting rate, pitch brands that match your audience, and never start work without written terms covering deliverables, payment and usage rights.
